Garden snail

The garden snail is a land snail found across Europe and many other regions.[1] It feeds on leaves, fruit and bark,[2] and it moves on a layer of mucus that protects its foot from sharp stones.

Shell[edit]

The shell grows in a spiral as the snail gets older.[3] Its colour ranges from brown to yellow,[4] and darker bands help the animal hide among dead leaves on the ground.

Behaviour[edit]

Garden snails are mostly active at night and after rain.[5] During dry weather they seal the shell opening with a thin epiphragm,[6] which keeps moisture inside until conditions improve again.

In winter they hibernate under logs or in soil.[7] Many gardeners see them as pests,[8] although thrushes and hedgehogs rely on them as an important source of food each spring.
